course.title: AP World History: Modern
course.description: Understand the people, ideas, and connections that shaped the world from c. 1200 to the present.
course.previewDescription: Explore how states rose, belief systems spread, trade networks connected regions, and revolutions reshaped societies from c. 1200 to the present.

unit.title: Global Conflict

lesson.title: Conducting World War II
lesson.summary: How governments mobilized for total war, how new technology increased civilian deaths, and how the atomic bomb ended the war.
learningGoals: Explain similarities and differences in how governments used a variety of methods to conduct war.
lesson.bigIdea: World War II was an even more total war than the first, targeting civilians on a massive scale and ending with the use of atomic weapons.
lesson.context: Both sides mobilized entire economies and societies, and new technologies made cities into battlefields.

sections.title: Mobilization and civilians

blocks.text: The United States converted factories to war production, and millions of women took industrial jobs. The Soviet Union moved factories east. Governments rationed goods and used propaganda.
Bombing destroyed cities across Europe and Asia. The war killed an estimated 70 to 85 million people, more than half of them civilians.

sections.takeaway: Civilians were both workers in the war effort and targets of attack.

sections.title: The atomic bomb

blocks.text: In August 1945, the United States dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, and Japan surrendered days later. Historians debate whether the bombs were necessary to end the war and what role the coming rivalry with the Soviet Union played.

blocks.title: Cause and effect
blocks.text: The decision to use the bomb led to Japan's surrender and opened a nuclear age that shaped the Cold War.

blocks.title: Common trap
blocks.text: Present historical debates as debates. A strong answer can weigh arguments without treating one side as settled fact.

sections.takeaway: The atomic bomb ended the war and began the nuclear age.
